newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: ECNZ secures NZ$1.4 billion contract revenue.
newsitem.headline: ECNZ secures NZ$1.4 billion contract revenue.

text.p: Electricity Corporation of New Zealand said on Thursday it had secured NZ$1.4 billion in revenue over the next five years from its long-term contracts.

General Manager of Marketing Peter Larsen said ECNZ's memorandum of understanding with the government required the corporation to offer set percentages of its firm capacity by tender through long-term contracts.

"On June 26, 1996, ECNZ invited 43 registered tenderers to tender for 32,796 gigawatt hours of electricity price contracts. This quantity was offered over five years in five separate tender rounds," he said.
The fifth and final tender round closed on September 17.

"We regard the tender as an overwhelming success. Some 94 percent of the total volume on offer was allocated to bidders," Larsen said. Similar to an auction, market supply and demand determined the price paid for the electricity hedge contracts.
He said the average clearing prices for all years were higher than the set reserve prices.

Larsen said that when New Zealand's competitive wholesale electricity market began from October 1, it was likely that spot prices would vary. "Spot prices are set every half hour and it is difficult to predict what the average level of the spot price
will be, particularly in the first year of operation," he said.

"Successful participation in the tender has guaranteed buyers the price they will pay for their electricity in the future, which reduces their exposure to spot price fluctuation, allowing better business planning."
Larsen added: "We now look forward to full participation in New Zealand's first fully competitive wholesale electricity market when it begins next month."
